response.justification: Broad, long-tenured full-stack engineer with genuine high-throughput experience (Sociomantic/dunnhumby micro-services handling millions of requests per second), strong craftsmanship practices (TDD, CI/CD, trunk-based development), and current hands-on work on AI-agent infrastructure and MCP tooling at a Staff title — which maps well to the AI-native mindset requirement. The main gap is the must-have 'strong Python': Python appears nowhere in the skills or project history, with depth concentrated in TypeScript/Node and DLang instead. Distributed-systems depth is real but dates to 2018–2020, and recent roles (Optilyz pricing, re:cinq full-stack) read as product engineering rather than large-scale architecture or technical strategy at scale. Stakeholder management, incident response, and on-call ownership are not evidenced anywhere in the resume. Worth a screen to probe Python fluency and distributed-systems recency, but not a clear yes on paper.
strengths: Proven high-throughput distributed systems work (millions of HTTP req/sec, low-latency async services)
Current hands-on AI-agent infrastructure and MCP/dev-tooling experience at Staff level
Deep engineering craftsmanship: TDD, CI/CD, testing frameworks authored, teaching/workshop track record
concerns: No evidence of Python anywhere, despite it being a must-have core language
Distributed-systems depth is 6+ years stale; recent roles are product/full-stack focused
No demonstrated stakeholder management, technical strategy ownership, or on-call/incident response
